at dampe.explanation: "At dampe" means "to steam", to send up steam, as hot things do: Kaffen damper (The coffee is steaming). It is also the word for cooking in steam: at dampe grøntsager (to steam vegetables).

sentence.da: Den varme suppe begynder at **dampe**, når låget løftes.
sentence.en: The hot soup starts to steam when the lid is lifted.

at danne.explanation: "At danne" means "to form", to make something come into being: at danne en regering (to form a government). It is also what nature does: Der dannes tåge om morgenen (Fog forms in the morning). For shaping clay or dough with your hands, use at forme (to shape).

sentence.da: Vand kan **danne** is, når det bliver meget koldt.
sentence.en: Water can form ice when it gets very cold.

at danse.explanation: "At danse" means "to dance", to move to music alone or with a partner. To say who with, use med (with): Jeg danser med Anna (I dance with Anna).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **danse** til musikken.
sentence.en: I want to dance to the music.

at date.explanation: "At date" means "to date", to see someone romantically, to get to know them better. For the day on a calendar, use en dato (a date on the calendar).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **date** en sød fyr.
sentence.en: She would like to date a nice guy.

at debattere.explanation: "At debattere" means "to debate", to talk openly about a question where people have different opinions, often in public or in the media: Vi debatterer skolereformen (We are debating the school reform). Among friends, at diskutere (to discuss) is the everyday word.

sentence.da: Politikerne skal **debattere** loven i Folketinget i morgen.
sentence.en: The politicians are going to debate the law in Parliament tomorrow.

at definere.explanation: "At definere" means "to define", to say exactly what a word or an idea means: Hvordan definerer du lykke? (How do you define happiness?) It is also used for setting something out clearly before you start: at definere et mål (to define a goal).

sentence.da: En ordbog hjælper dig med at **definere** ukendte ord.
sentence.en: A dictionary helps you define unknown words.

at dele.explanation: "At dele" means "to share": Jeg deler min mad med dig (I share my food with you). It also means "to divide", as in math: ti delt med to (ten divided by two).

sentence.da: Vi vil **dele** en pizza.
sentence.en: We want to share a pizza.

at dele ud.explanation: "At dele ud" means "to hand out", giving things to several people: Læreren deler papirer ud (The teacher hands out papers). Plain at dele means "to share": Vi deler en pizza (We share a pizza).

sentence.da: Han skal **dele ud** til alle børnene.
sentence.en: He is going to hand things out to all the children.

at delegere.explanation: "At delegere" means "to delegate", to hand a task or some power to someone else to handle. A leader does it: Chefen delegerer opgaver til sine medarbejdere (The boss delegates tasks to the staff). The person who gets the task follows til (to): Hun delegerer opgaven til Lars (She delegates the task to Lars).

sentence.da: En god leder tør **delegere** ansvar til andre.
sentence.en: A good leader dares to delegate responsibility to others.

at deltage.explanation: "At deltage" means "to participate" or "to take part", and you add i (in) before the event: Jeg deltager i mødet (I am taking part in the meeting).

sentence.da: Alle kan **deltage** i kurset gratis.
sentence.en: Everyone can take part in the course for free.

at demonstrere.explanation: "At demonstrere" means "to demonstrate", to show how something works: Læreren demonstrerer forsøget (The teacher demonstrates the experiment). It also means to take part in a protest: Folk demonstrerer foran Christiansborg (People are demonstrating in front of Christiansborg).

sentence.da: Hun vil **demonstrere**, hvordan maskinen virker.
sentence.en: She will demonstrate how the machine works.

at designe.explanation: "At designe" means "to design", to plan how something will look and work before it is made: Hun designer smykker (She designs jewelry).

sentence.da: Arkitekten skal **designe** et nyt hus.
sentence.en: The architect is going to design a new house.

at dirigere.explanation: "At dirigere" means "to conduct" an orchestra, and "to direct" people or traffic: Politiet dirigerer trafikken (The police are directing traffic). For directing a film, use at instruere (to direct a film) instead.

sentence.da: Han skal **dirigere** koret ved koncerten i aften.
sentence.en: He is going to conduct the choir at the concert tonight.

at diskutere.explanation: "At diskutere" means "to discuss": Vi diskuterer planen (We are discussing the plan). For an angry fight, use at skændes (to quarrel): De skændes hele tiden (They quarrel all the time).

sentence.da: Vi skal **diskutere** problemet med læreren.
sentence.en: We have to discuss the problem with the teacher.

at distrahere.explanation: "At distrahere" means "to distract", to take someone's attention away from what they are doing: Støjen distraherer mig (The noise distracts me). It can be done on purpose: Tyven distraherede vagten (The thief distracted the guard).

sentence.da: Telefonen kan **distrahere** dig, når du laver lektier.
sentence.en: The phone can distract you when you do homework.

at dividere.explanation: "At dividere" means "to divide" in math: Jeg dividerer ti med to (I divide ten by two). To share something between people, say at dele (to share).

sentence.da: Du skal **dividere** tolv med tre.
sentence.en: You have to divide twelve by three.

at dokumentere.explanation: "At dokumentere" means "to document", to show with papers, photos or numbers that something is true or has happened: Politiet kan dokumentere, hvad der skete (The police can document what happened).

sentence.da: Du skal **dokumentere** dine udgifter med kvitteringer.
sentence.en: You must document your expenses with receipts.

at dominere.explanation: "At dominere" means "to dominate", to be the strongest or most noticeable part of something. A person can do it in a conversation: Han dominerer samtalen (He dominates the conversation). A color can do it too: Blå dominerer billedet (Blue dominates the picture).

sentence.da: Det bedste hold kan **dominere** kampen fra første minut.
sentence.en: The best team can dominate the match from the first minute.

at donere.explanation: "At donere" means "to donate", to give money, things, blood or organs without getting anything in return. The one who gets it comes after til (to): Jeg donerer penge til Røde Kors (I donate money to the Red Cross).

sentence.da: Mange vil gerne **donere** blod, fordi det kan redde liv.
sentence.en: Many people want to donate blood because it can save lives.

at downloade.explanation: "At downloade" means "to download", to copy something from the internet onto your own device: Jeg downloader appen (I download the app).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **downloade** en film til min telefon.
sentence.en: I want to download a movie to my phone.

at drage.explanation: "At drage" means "to draw" in set phrases such as at drage en konklusion (to draw a conclusion), and "to go" when someone sets out on a journey, in an old-fashioned, storybook way: Han drog ud i verden (He set out into the world). For an ordinary trip, people say at tage af sted (to leave).

sentence.da: Efter testen kan vi **drage** en klar konklusion.
sentence.en: After the test, we can draw a clear conclusion.

at dreje.explanation: "At dreje" means "to turn": Drej til højre (Turn right). With sig om (about) it means "to be about": Det drejer sig om penge (It is about money).

sentence.da: Du skal **dreje** til venstre ved banken.
sentence.en: You have to turn left at the bank.

at drikke.explanation: "At drikke" means "to drink", for water, coffee, beer and so on: Jeg drikker kaffe (I drink coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **drikke** et glas vand.
sentence.en: I want to drink a glass of water.

at drille.explanation: "At drille" means "to tease", usually in a playful way: Han driller sin lillesøster (He teases his little sister). Hurtful teasing is more like at mobbe (to bully).

sentence.da: Min bror elsker at **drille** mig.
sentence.en: My brother loves to tease me.

at drive.explanation: "At drive" means "to run" a business: at drive en butik (to run a shop). It also means "to drift" with wind or water: Skyerne driver hen over himlen (The clouds drift across the sky).

sentence.da: Hun vil **drive** sin egen café på havnen.
sentence.en: She wants to run her own cafe at the harbor.

at droppe.explanation: "At droppe" means "to drop" a plan or "to skip" something: Jeg dropper festen (I am skipping the party).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **droppe** sukker i min kaffe.
sentence.en: I want to skip sugar in my coffee.

at drukne.explanation: "At drukne" means "to drown", to die by being under water and not being able to breathe: Manden druknede i søen (The man drowned in the lake).

sentence.da: Man kan **drukne** i dybt vand.
sentence.en: You can drown in deep water.

at dryppe.explanation: "At dryppe" means "to drip", to fall in single drops: Taget drypper efter regnen (The roof is dripping after the rain). It also means to put drops on something: at dryppe citron på fisken (to drip lemon on the fish).

sentence.da: Hanen i køkkenet kan **dryppe** hele natten.
sentence.en: The tap in the kitchen can drip all night.

at drysse.explanation: "At drysse" means "to sprinkle", to let small pieces fall lightly over something: at drysse sukker på kagen (to sprinkle sugar on the cake). For light snow or rain, Danes say Det drysser (It is sprinkling).

sentence.da: Man kan **drysse** kanel over risengrød.
sentence.en: You can sprinkle cinnamon over rice pudding.

at dræbe.explanation: "At dræbe" means "to kill": Katten dræbte musen (The cat killed the mouse). To say someone was killed, use blev dræbt: Han blev dræbt (He was killed).

sentence.da: Ræven kan **dræbe** en høne.
sentence.en: The fox can kill a hen.

at drøfte.explanation: "At drøfte" means "to discuss", to talk something through carefully, for example in a meeting: Vi drøfter budgettet på mandag (We are discussing the budget on Monday). It takes the topic directly, unlike at tale om (to talk about).

sentence.da: Bestyrelsen skal **drøfte** forslaget på næste møde.
sentence.en: The board must discuss the proposal at the next meeting.

at drømme.explanation: "At drømme" means "to dream", both asleep and awake, and it takes om (about): Jeg drømte om dig (I dreamed about you). Hun drømmer om et stort hus (She dreams of a big house).

sentence.da: Jeg vil sove og **drømme** hele natten.
sentence.en: I want to sleep and dream all night.

at dufte.explanation: "At dufte" means "to smell nice": Blomsterne dufter dejligt (The flowers smell lovely). Plain at lugte (to smell) can also be bad: Det lugter af fisk (It smells like fish).

sentence.da: Det plejer at **dufte** dejligt her.
sentence.en: It usually smells lovely here.

at duge.explanation: "At duge" means "to be any good", to be good enough for a purpose. It is mostly used in the negative: Det duer ikke (That will not do). Careful, duer also means doves (en due is a dove), so context decides.

forms.en: I have been any good / worked

sentence.da: Den gamle cykel vil ikke **duge** til så lang en tur.
sentence.en: The old bike will not do for such a long trip.

at dukke op.explanation: "At dukke op" means "to show up", often when someone arrives or something appears unexpectedly: Han dukkede op klokken otte (He showed up at eight o'clock). On a screen it means "to pop up": En besked dukker op (A message pops up).

sentence.da: Jeg håber, at han vil **dukke op** i aften.
sentence.en: I hope that he will show up tonight.

at dumpe.explanation: "At dumpe" means "to fail (an exam)": Han dumpede til eksamen (He failed the exam). The opposite is at bestå (to pass): Hun bestod eksamen (She passed the exam).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **dumpe** til eksamen.
sentence.en: I don't want to fail the exam.

at dykke.explanation: "At dykke" means "to dive" under water: Børnene dykker efter sten (The children dive for stones). To dive in headfirst from a board, say at stupe (to dive in): Han stuper fra vippen (He dives from the board).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **dykke** og se fiskene i havet.
sentence.en: I would like to dive and see the fish in the sea.

at dyppe.explanation: "At dyppe" means "to dip", to put something briefly into a liquid or a sauce and take it out again: Jeg dypper brødet i suppen (I dip the bread in the soup). The dip is short, unlike at lægge i blød (to soak).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker at **dyppe** pommes frites i ketchup.
sentence.en: The children love to dip french fries in ketchup.

at dyrke.explanation: "At dyrke" means "to grow" plants on purpose: Vi dyrker tomater (We grow tomatoes). It also means "to practice" a sport or hobby: Jeg dyrker yoga (I do yoga).

sentence.da: Min mor vil **dyrke** grøntsager i haven.
sentence.en: My mother wants to grow vegetables in the garden.

at dyrke sport.explanation: "At dyrke sport" means "to do sports" as a regular activity: Jeg dyrker sport hver uge (I do sports every week). For one sport, Danes often use at spille: Jeg spiller tennis (I play tennis).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **dyrke sport** mere i år.
sentence.en: I want to do more sports this year.

at dække.explanation: "At dække" means "to cover": Jeg dækker bordet med en dug (I cover the table with a cloth). At dække bord means "to set the table". It also works for costs: Forsikringen dækker skaden (The insurance covers the damage).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **dække** barnet med et tæppe.
sentence.en: I want to cover the child with a blanket.

at dække bord.explanation: "At dække bord" means "to set the table", putting the plates out before a meal: Kan du dække bord? (Can you set the table?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal **dække bord** til fem personer.
sentence.en: I have to set the table for five people.

at dække over.explanation: "At dække over" means "to cover up", to keep a mistake or a crime from coming out. With a person, dække over nogen means to stay quiet for them: Hun dækkede over sin bror (She covered for her brother).

sentence.da: Han ville **dække over** fejlen, men sandheden kom frem.
sentence.en: He wanted to cover up the mistake, but the truth came out.

at dæmpe.explanation: "At dæmpe" means "to dampen", to make a sound, a light or a feeling weaker: at dæmpe lyset (to dim the light). Said to a person, Dæmp dig! (Tone it down!)

sentence.da: Du må gerne **dæmpe** musikken, når naboerne sover.
sentence.en: You may turn the music down when the neighbors are asleep.

at dø.explanation: "At dø" means "to die". For "have died" Danish uses er (am / is), not har (have): Han er død (He has died).

sentence.da: Planter kan **dø** uden vand.
sentence.en: Plants can die without water.

at døbe.explanation: "At døbe" means "to baptize", to welcome a person into the Christian church with water, and to give a baby its name: Hun blev døbt Maria (She was baptized Maria). It is also used for giving a name to something: Vi døbte hunden Bølle (We named the dog Bølle).

sentence.da: Præsten skal **døbe** barnet på søndag.
sentence.en: The priest will baptize the child on Sunday.

at dømme.explanation: "At dømme" means "to judge" and "to sentence". In a court, it means to find someone guilty and set the punishment. Outside court, it is about forming an opinion of someone: Man skal ikke dømme folk på udseendet (You should not judge people by their looks).

sentence.da: Retten kan **dømme** ham til to års fængsel.
sentence.en: The court can sentence him to two years in prison.

da.explanation: "Da" means "when", for something that happened once in the past. For now or later, use når (when) instead: Når jeg kommer hjem, sover børnene (When I get home, the children are asleep).

sentence.da: **Da** jeg kom hjem, sov børnene.
sentence.en: When I came home, the children were asleep.

dagen efter.explanation: "Dagen efter" means "the day after" something that was just mentioned. On its own, the next day is næste dag.

forms.en: The day after, he came home

sentence.da: Jeg var træt **dagen efter** festen.
sentence.en: I was tired the day after the party.

dagens ret.explanation: "Dagens ret" means "dish of the day". Word for word, it is the day's dish: dagens (the day's) and ret (dish).

sentence.da: **Dagens ret** er fisk og kartofler.
sentence.en: The dish of the day is fish and potatoes.

dagevis.explanation: "Dagevis" means "for days", one after another over a long stretch. The ending -vis marks a long stretch, as in timevis (for hours) and ugevis (for weeks).

sentence.da: Efter stormen var der **dagevis** uden strøm.
sentence.en: After the storm there was no power for days.

daglig.explanation: "Daglig" means "daily" and goes before a thing that happens every day. For an action, use hver dag (every day) instead: Jeg løber hver dag (I run every day).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **daglig** gåtur.
sentence.en: I take a daily walk.

dagligdags.explanation: "Dagligdags" means "everyday" and describes ordinary things that happen all the time. It also fits language: dagligdags sprog (everyday language).

sentence.da: Indkøb og madlavning er **dagligdags** ting.
sentence.en: Shopping and cooking are everyday things.

dagligt.explanation: "Dagligt" means "daily" or "every day". It stays dagligt after a verb or before an et-word: et dagligt møde (a daily meeting). Before an en-word it becomes daglig: en daglig tur (a daily walk).

sentence.da: Han træner **dagligt** og spiser sundt.
sentence.en: He trains daily and eats healthily.

dagligvarer.explanation: "Dagligvarer" means "groceries": everyday goods like food and household things. It is built from daglig (daily) and varer (goods) and is almost always plural.

sentence.da: Jeg køber **dagligvarer** i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: I buy groceries at the supermarket.

dagpenge.explanation: "Dagpenge" means "unemployment benefits", money you get each day when you are out of work. You only get them if you have been a member of an a-kasse (an unemployment insurance fund). The word is always plural and literally means "day money".

sentence.da: Når man bliver fyret, kan man få **dagpenge** i en periode.
sentence.en: When you get fired, you can get unemployment benefits for a period.

dagslys.explanation: "Dagslys" means "daylight", the natural light you have while the sun is up, even on a cloudy day. Light from a lamp is not dagslys.

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der kun få timer med **dagslys**.
sentence.en: In winter there are only a few hours of daylight.

damp.explanation: "Damp" means "steam", the hot cloud from boiling water. It is also what makes mirrors and windows misty.

forms.en: There is steam in the bathroom.

sentence.da: Når vand koger, bliver det til **damp**.
sentence.en: When water boils, it turns into steam.

dansk.explanation: "Dansk" means "Danish", the language and also things from Denmark. As a school subject, it is used without en or et: Jeg har dansk (I have Danish class). Language names start with a small letter: dansk (Danish), engelsk (English).

sentence.da: Jeg bor i Danmark og taler **dansk**.
sentence.en: I live in Denmark and speak Danish.

data.explanation: "Data" means "data", facts and numbers collected for a purpose, for example in research or on a computer.

sentence.da: Vi bruger **data** fra mange mennesker.
sentence.en: We use data from many people.

datalogi.explanation: "Datalogi" means "computer science", the science of how data is stored and processed and how programs are made. It is the name of the university subject. In everyday talk, computer work is just called IT.

sentence.da: Hun læser **datalogi** og lærer at skrive programmer.
sentence.en: She studies computer science and learns to write programs.

datid.explanation: "En datid" means "past tense", the form of a word that tells you something has already happened. For the past as a period of history, the usual word is fortid (the past).

forms.da: datiden af at gå er gik
forms.en: the past tense of at gå is gik

sentence.da: Ordet spiste står i **datid**, fordi det allerede er sket.
sentence.en: The word spiste is in the past tense because it has already happened.

davs.explanation: "Davs" means "hi", a short, casual greeting for people you know. Hej (hi) is the everyday greeting that suits everyone.

sentence.da: **Davs**, Peter! Hvordan går det?
sentence.en: Hi, Peter! How is it going?

de.explanation: "De" means "they". Compare De ser mig (They see me) with Jeg ser dem (I see them), where dem means "them". De is also "the" before many things: de store huse (the big houses).

sentence.da: Anna og Lars? **De** er hjemme.
sentence.en: Anna and Lars? They are at home.

december.explanation: "December" means "December". Danish writes month names with a small letter, so you write i december (in December), not i December.

sentence.da: Vi fejrer jul i **december**.
sentence.en: We celebrate Christmas in December.

dedikeret.explanation: "Dedikeret" means "dedicated", for a person who gives a lot of time and effort to a job or cause. It can also mean made for one use only: en dedikeret server (a dedicated server).

sentence.da: Hun er en **dedikeret** lærer og bruger mange timer på sine elever.
sentence.en: She is a dedicated teacher and spends many hours on her pupils.

defekt.explanation: "Defekt" means "defective", for a machine or part that does not work as it should. In everyday speech, ødelagt (broken) is also common.

sentence.da: Vaskemaskinen er **defekt**, og den vil ikke starte.
sentence.en: The washing machine is defective, and it will not start.

dejlig.explanation: "Dejlig" means "lovely" or "nice" and is a warm word for things you enjoy, like weather, food or a day.

sentence.da: Det er en **dejlig** varm sommerdag.
sentence.en: It is a lovely warm summer day.

dels ... dels.explanation: "Dels ... dels" means "partly ... partly", for listing two reasons or sides that each matter. At the start of a sentence, the verb comes right after dels: Dels er det dyrt, dels er det svært (Partly it is expensive, partly it is hard).

forms.da: dels for sjov, dels for pengene
forms.en: partly for fun, partly for the money
partly at home, partly at the office

related.da: på den ene side ... på den anden side
related.en: on the one hand ... on the other

sentence.da: Hvorfor jeg bor her? **Dels ... dels**: jobbet og familien.
sentence.en: Why do I live here? Partly ... partly: the job and the family.

deltagelse.explanation: "Deltagelse" means "participation", being involved in an event, a class or a project. It takes i (in) before the event: deltagelse i kurset (participation in the course).

sentence.da: Din **deltagelse** i mødet er vigtig for os.
sentence.en: Your participation in the meeting is important to us.

dem.explanation: "Dem" means "them". Compare De ser mig (They see me) with Jeg ser dem (I see them): de (they) is for the ones doing it, dem for the ones it happens to.

sentence.da: Mine naboer er søde. Jeg kender **dem**.
sentence.en: My neighbors are nice. I know them.

demokratisk.explanation: "Demokratisk" means "democratic", for a country, group or decision where the people decide, usually by voting. It also describes a way of working where everyone gets an equal say.

sentence.da: I et **demokratisk** land vælger folket selv sine politikere.
sentence.en: In a democratic country, the people choose their own politicians.

den.explanation: "Den" means "it" for words that take en. Compare Jeg har en bil. Den er rød (I have a car. It is red) with Jeg har et hus. Det er rødt (I have a house. It is red). Den also means "the" before a describing word: den store bil (the big car).

sentence.da: Se på bilen! **Den** er meget stor.
sentence.en: Look at the car! It is very big.

den offentlige sektor.explanation: "Den offentlige sektor" means "the public sector", all the work paid for by taxes: offices, hospitals, schools and local councils. The part run by companies is den private sektor (the private sector).

forms.da: at arbejde i den offentlige sektor
forms.en: to work in the public sector

sentence.da: Lærere og sygeplejersker arbejder i **den offentlige sektor**.
sentence.en: Teachers and nurses work in the public sector.

den tid, den sorg.explanation: "Den tid, den sorg" means "cross that bridge when we come to it": do not stress about a problem before it actually happens. Word for word, it says that a later time brings its own sorrow. People say it to wave away a concern about something that may never happen.

forms.en: We'll cross that bridge when we come to it

forms.da: Det tager vi, når det sker
forms.en: We'll deal with that when it happens

forms.da: Hvad hvis det går galt? Den tid, den sorg
forms.en: What if it goes wrong? We'll cross that bridge when we come to it

sentence.da: Måske bliver det dyrt senere, men **den tid, den sorg**.
sentence.en: Maybe it will get expensive later, but we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.

dengang.explanation: "Dengang" means "back then" and always points to the past. It is built from den (that) and gang (time), so it literally means "that time".

forms.en: What were you doing back then?
My father lived here back then.

sentence.da: **Dengang** boede vi i Odense og var glade.
sentence.en: Back then we lived in Odense and were happy.

denim.explanation: "Denim" means "denim", the strong, usually blue cloth that jeans are made of. Jeans are often called cowboybukser (cowboy pants) in Danish.

sentence.da: Jakken er af **denim**, og den holder i mange år.
sentence.en: The jacket is made of denim, and it lasts for many years.

denne.explanation: "Denne" means "this" with words that take en. Compare denne bil (this car) with dette hus (this house, as hus takes et). It sounds formal; in everyday speech people say den her bil (this car).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **denne** bil.
sentence.en: I want this car.

dens.explanation: "Dens" means "its" and belongs to something that is an en-word, like a car or a chair. For an et-word, like a house, use dets.

sentence.da: Bilen er gammel, men **dens** motor er stærk.
sentence.en: The car is old, but its engine is strong.

deprimerende.explanation: "Deprimerende" means "depressing", something that pulls your mood down and makes you feel low and without hope. It describes the cause, while deprimeret (depressed) describes the person who feels it.

sentence.da: Regnen og mørket om vinteren kan være **deprimerende**.
sentence.en: The rain and darkness in winter can be depressing.

deprimeret.explanation: "Deprimeret" means "depressed", feeling very low and without energy or hope. It can be a passing mood or a medical condition. It describes the person who feels it, while deprimerende (depressing) describes the cause.

sentence.da: Han føler sig **deprimeret** og har ikke lyst til at se nogen.
sentence.en: He feels depressed and does not want to see anyone.

der.explanation: "Der" means "there". Compare Han er her (He is here) with Han er der (He is there). At the start of a sentence, der says something exists: Der er mange børn (There are many children). It can also mean "who": manden, der bor her (the man who lives here).

sentence.da: **Der** er en kat i haven.
sentence.en: There is a cat in the garden.

der er ingen ko på isen.explanation: "Der er ingen ko på isen" means "there's nothing to worry about": the danger is over or never existed. Word for word, it says there is no cow on the ice. The opposite is Der er ko på isen (There is trouble).

forms.da: Der er ingen ko på isen
forms.en: There is nothing to worry about

forms.da: Rolig, der er ingen ko på isen
Der er ingen ko på isen, vi har god tid
forms.en: There's nothing to worry about, we have plenty of time

sentence.da: Alt er klaret, og **der er ingen ko på isen**.
sentence.en: Everything is taken care of, and there is nothing to worry about.

derefter.explanation: "Derefter" means "after that". Compare efter maden (after the meal), where efter needs a word after it, with derefter (after that), which stands alone.

sentence.da: Først mad, og **derefter** kaffe.
sentence.en: First food, and after that coffee.

deres.explanation: "Deres" means "their". Compare Det er hans hus (It is his house) with Det er deres hus (It is their house). It stays the same for one thing or many: deres hund (their dog), deres hunde (their dogs).

sentence.da: Anna og Bo bor i **deres** hus.
sentence.en: Anna and Bo live in their house.

derfor.explanation: "Derfor" means "that is why". The same fact can be said two ways: Jeg er syg, derfor bliver jeg hjemme (I am sick, that is why I am staying home) and Jeg bliver hjemme, fordi jeg er syg (I am staying home because I am sick).

forms.en: that is why I am here

sentence.da: Det regner. **Derfor** er jeg hjemme.
sentence.en: It is raining. That is why I am home.

derfra.explanation: "Derfra" means "from there" and tells where something comes from, a place away from you. Compare Jeg kommer herfra (I come from here) with Jeg kommer derfra (I come from there).

forms.en: What can you see from there?

sentence.da: Aarhus er flot. Min mor kommer **derfra**.
sentence.en: Aarhus is beautiful. My mother comes from there.

derhen.explanation: "Derhen" means "(to) there" and is used when you move toward a place. To say where someone is, use der (there): Han er der (He is there).

sentence.da: Skal vi gå **derhen** sammen?
sentence.en: Shall we walk there together?

derhjemme.explanation: "Derhjemme" means "at home", said about your home when you are not in it or about life there in general: Derhjemme har vi to katte (At home we have two cats). Compare Jeg er hjemme (I am at home, right now).

forms.en: what do you do at home?

sentence.da: **Derhjemme** spiser vi sent.
sentence.en: At home we eat late.

derimod.explanation: "Derimod" means "on the other hand", showing a contrast with what was just said. It stands near the thing you compare: Jeg kan ikke lide kaffe. Te kan jeg derimod godt lide (I do not like coffee. Tea, on the other hand, I like).

forms.da: Prisen er høj. Kvaliteten derimod er god.
forms.en: The price is high. The quality, on the other hand, is good.
You, on the other hand, are right

sentence.da: Byen er larmende. Landet er **derimod** stille.
sentence.en: The city is noisy. The countryside, on the other hand, is quiet.

derinde.explanation: "Derinde" means "in there" and points to a place inside something, away from you, such as another room. Compare Jeg er herinde (I am in here) with Katten er derinde (The cat is in there).

forms.en: in there in the living room

sentence.da: Min mor er **derinde** i stuen.
sentence.en: My mother is in there in the living room.

dermed.explanation: "Dermed" means "thereby" and "with that", linking a result to what was just said. It is built from der (there) and med (with). In casual talk, så (so) is more common.

sentence.da: Vi har betalt, og **dermed** er sagen afgjort.
sentence.en: We have paid, and with that the matter is settled.

dernede.explanation: "Dernede" means "down there" and points to a place lower than you, away from you, such as a basement or the floor below. Compare Katten er deroppe (The cat is up there) with Katten er dernede (The cat is down there).

sentence.da: Bilen står **dernede** i kælderen.
sentence.en: The car is down there in the basement.

dernæst.explanation: "Dernæst" means "next" and "then", for the next step in a series. It fits instructions, speeches and lists, where it follows først (first).

sentence.da: Først skærer du løget, og **dernæst** steger du det i smør.
sentence.en: First you cut the onion, and then you fry it in butter.

deroppe.explanation: "Deroppe" means "up there" and tells where something is when it is higher than you and away from you. It is built from der (there) and oppe (up).

forms.en: The cat is sitting up there

sentence.da: Kan du se fuglen **deroppe** i træet?
sentence.en: Can you see the bird up there in the tree?

derovre.explanation: "Derovre" means "over there", for a place at a distance that you can point to: Bogen ligger derovre (The book is over there). To move there, use derover: Jeg går derover (I am going over there).

sentence.da: Min bil står **derovre** ved huset.
sentence.en: My car is parked over there by the house.

derude.explanation: "Derude" means "out there" and points to a place outside or farther out, away from you. Compare Børnene er derinde (The children are in there) with Børnene er derude (The children are out there).

sentence.da: Se ud af vinduet! Børnene leger **derude**.
sentence.en: Look out of the window! The children are playing out there.

derudover.explanation: "Derudover" means "in addition", adding one more point to what you just said. At the start of a sentence, the verb follows right after it.

forms.en: In addition, we have a garden

sentence.da: Han arbejder på kontoret, og **derudover** passer han en lille butik.
sentence.en: He works at an office, and in addition he runs a small shop.

design.explanation: "Design" means "design", how something is planned to look and work, like a chair, a phone or a website. It is also a job field: Hun arbejder med design (She works in design).

sentence.da: Jeg kan lide stolens **design** og farve.
sentence.en: I like the chair's design and color.

desperat.explanation: "Desperat" means "desperate", for a person who sees no way out or for what they do. To say what someone is desperate for, use efter (for): Hun er desperat efter et job (She is desperate for a job).

sentence.da: Han var **desperat** og ringede til alle.
sentence.en: He was desperate and called everyone.

desto.explanation: "Desto" means "the" in a pair like "the more..., the better". It comes in the second half, after jo in the first: Jo mere du øver, desto bedre bliver du (The more you practice, the better you get).

sentence.da: Jo ældre vinen er, **desto** dyrere bliver den.
sentence.en: The older the wine is, the more expensive it gets.

desuden.explanation: "Desuden" means "furthermore" and "besides" and adds one more point to what you just said, often a final reason.

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, og **desuden** er det sent.
sentence.en: I am tired, and besides, it is late.

desværre.explanation: "Desværre" means "unfortunately". Use it before bad news or a no. It sounds softer and more polite than just Nej (No).

sentence.da: **Desværre** har jeg ikke tid i dag.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, I do not have time today.

det.explanation: "Det" means "it" or "that". Use it for a thing that takes et: Jeg har et hus, og det er stort (I have a house, and it is big). Things that take en use den: Jeg har en bil, og den er stor (I have a car, and it is big). Det is also used for weather and general statements: Det regner (It is raining), Det er sjovt (That is fun).

forms.en: I know it / I know that.

sentence.da: Se på huset! **Det** er meget gammelt.
sentence.en: Look at the house! It is very old.

det er.explanation: "Det er" means "it is" or "that is"; Danish uses the same two words for both. Use it to name things or describe them.

sentence.da: **Det er** en god dag i dag.
sentence.en: It is a good day today.

det er en god idé.explanation: "Det er en god idé" means "that's a good idea", said to agree with a suggestion. You can shorten it to God idé! (Good idea!).

sentence.da: Café i dag? **Det er en god idé.**
sentence.en: Cafe today? That's a good idea.

det er fint med mig.explanation: "Det er fint med mig" means "that's fine with me" and agrees to a plan. Change mig to dig (you) to ask: Er det fint med dig? (Is that fine with you?).

forms.da: Ja, det er fint med mig.
Hvis det er fint med dig.

sentence.da: Vi ses klokken fem? **Det er fint med mig.**
sentence.en: See you at five? That's fine with me.

det er hip som hap.explanation: "Det er hip som hap" means "it's six of one, half a dozen of the other": two choices are about equal. Say it when you are asked to choose and you do not mind: Kaffe eller te? Det er hip som hap (Coffee or tea? Either is fine).

forms.da: Det er hip som hap, hvad vi vælger
forms.en: It's all the same what we choose

forms.da: Det er hip som hap, om vi går nu eller senere
forms.en: It makes no difference whether we go now or later

sentence.da: **Det er hip som hap**, fordi bussen og toget koster det samme.
sentence.en: It's all the same, because the bus and the train cost the same.

det er i orden.explanation: "Det er i orden" means "it's okay" or "that's fine". Danes say it in reply to undskyld (sorry) and to agree to a plan. I orden literally means "in order".

sentence.da: Undskyld! — **Det er i orden.**
sentence.en: Sorry! — It's okay.

det er ikke så svært.explanation: "Det er ikke så svært" means "it's not that hard". Svært means "difficult" and "ikke så" means "not so".

sentence.da: Dansk? **Det er ikke så svært.**
sentence.en: Danish? It's not that hard.

det er lige det.explanation: "Det er lige det" means "that's exactly it" and you say it when someone has hit the right point. Lige det alone means "exactly that": Jeg ville have lige det (I wanted exactly that).

forms.da: Det er lige det, jeg mener
Nej, det er ikke lige det

sentence.da: Præcis, **det er lige det**, jeg mener.
sentence.en: Exactly, that's just what I mean.

det er lige meget.explanation: "Det er lige meget" means "it doesn't matter". Use it when you are happy with any choice. Careful with tone: Det er mig lige meget (I don't care) can sound rude, so say det gør ikke noget (it's no problem) when you want to be kind.

forms.da: Det er lige meget, hvad du vælger.
forms.en: It doesn't matter what you choose.

sentence.da: Te eller kaffe? **Det er lige meget.**
sentence.en: Tea or coffee? It doesn't matter.

det er min skyld.explanation: "Det er min skyld" means "it's my fault" and takes the blame. Change min (my) to hans (his) to blame someone else: Det er hans skyld (It's his fault).

sentence.da: Jeg glemte at ringe, **det er min skyld**.
sentence.en: I forgot to call, it's my fault.

det er rigtigt.explanation: "Det er rigtigt" means "that's right", said to agree that something is correct or true. Be careful: rigtig also means "really" before another word, as in rigtig godt (really good). A short alternative is ja, præcis (yes, exactly).

sentence.da: Du bor i Aarhus? **Det er rigtigt.**
sentence.en: You live in Aarhus? That's right.

det er synd.explanation: "Det er synd" means "that's a shame" or "that's too bad", and shows sympathy when something goes wrong. To say you feel sorry for someone, add for and the person: Det er synd for ham (I feel sorry for him).

sentence.da: Du kan ikke komme? **Det er synd!**
sentence.en: You can't come? That's a shame!

det giver ikke mening.explanation: "Det giver ikke mening" means "that doesn't make sense". Word for word, it says that gives no meaning. For something you cannot follow, you can also say Jeg forstår det ikke (I don't understand).

forms.en: That makes no sense at all

sentence.da: Du siger ja og nej, og **det giver ikke mening**.
sentence.en: You say yes and no, and that doesn't make sense.

det giver mening.explanation: "Det giver mening" means "that makes sense". The word mening (meaning, sense) also means "opinion": Hvad er din mening? (What is your opinion?).

sentence.da: Nu forstår jeg, og **det giver mening**.
sentence.en: Now I understand, and that makes sense.

det går fint.explanation: "Det går fint" means "it's going fine" and is a common answer to Hvordan går det? (How is it going?). Swap fint (fine) for godt (well) or dårligt (badly) to change the mood.

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? **Det går fint.**
sentence.en: How is it going? It's going fine.

det går godt.explanation: "Det går godt" means "it's going well" and is a standard answer to Hvordan går det? (How's it going?). After answering, it is polite to ask og dig? (and you?).

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? **Det går godt.**
sentence.en: How is it going? It's going well.

det gør ikke noget.explanation: "Det gør ikke noget" means "it's okay" or "no problem", what you say when someone says Undskyld (Sorry). Word for word, it says it does not do anything. Do not mix it up with det er lige meget (it doesn't matter), which is for choices.

forms.da: Det gør ikke noget, jeg venter.

sentence.da: "Undskyld!" – "**Det gør ikke noget.**"
sentence.en: "Sorry!" – "It's okay."

det håber jeg.explanation: "Det håber jeg" means "I hope so", a short reply to a question about something that might happen.

sentence.da: Bliver det godt vejr? **Det håber jeg.**
sentence.en: Will the weather be good? I hope so.

det kan godt være.explanation: "Det kan godt være" means "that may be" and admits something could be true, often before you add men (but) and say what you think instead.

forms.da: Det kan godt være, du har ret.
forms.en: That may be, you could be right.

sentence.da: **Det kan godt være**, men jeg ser det anderledes.
sentence.en: That may be, but I see it differently.

det kan man ikke vide.explanation: "Det kan man ikke vide" means "you never know" and is said when the future is uncertain. Literally it says that one cannot know it.

sentence.da: Måske bliver det godt. **Det kan man ikke vide**.
sentence.en: Maybe it will be good. You never know.

det kommer an på.explanation: "Det kommer an på" means "it depends". Always follow it with på (on) and then what it depends on.

sentence.da: **Det kommer an på**, hvor meget det koster.
sentence.en: It depends on how much it costs.

det lyder godt.explanation: "Det lyder godt" means "that sounds good". Use it to react positively to a plan, an offer or an idea. At lyde means "to sound".

sentence.da: Middag klokken seks? **Det lyder godt.**
sentence.en: Dinner at six? That sounds good.

det passer.explanation: "Det passer" means "that's true" and confirms a fact. Add ikke to say the opposite: Det passer ikke (That's not true).

sentence.da: Du er fra Norge, ikke? Ja, **det passer**.
sentence.en: You are from Norway, right? Yes, that's true.

det passer ikke.explanation: "Det passer ikke" means "that's not true" and corrects a false claim. Without ikke (not) it says the claim is true.

sentence.da: **Det passer ikke**, jeg var der ikke i går.
sentence.en: That's not true, I wasn't there yesterday.

det tror jeg.explanation: "Det tror jeg" means "I think so" or "I believe so", a polite, slightly unsure reply when you aren't completely certain.

sentence.da: Er han hjemme? **Det tror jeg.**
sentence.en: Is he home? I think so.

det tror jeg ikke.explanation: "Det tror jeg ikke" means "I don't think so", a soft way to say no. Word for word, it is that think I not. It sounds gentler than a plain nej (no).

sentence.da: Regner det i dag? **Det tror jeg ikke.**
sentence.en: Is it raining today? I don't think so.

det var dog utroligt.explanation: "Det var dog utroligt" means "that's incredible" and reacts to surprising or impressive news. The little word dog (though) adds surprise; without it, Det var utroligt (That was incredible) sounds calmer.

sentence.da: Hun vandt tre gange i træk, **det var dog utroligt**!
sentence.en: She won three times in a row, that's incredible!

det var på høje tid.explanation: "Det var på høje tid" means "it was high time": something should have happened earlier and cannot wait any longer. It often sounds a little impatient: Det var på høje tid, at du kom! (It was high time you showed up!)

forms.da: Nu er det på høje tid at gå
forms.en: Now it is high time to go

sentence.da: Taget lækkede i årevis, og **det var på høje tid** at skifte det.
sentence.en: The roof leaked for years, and it was high time to replace it.

det var så lidt.explanation: "Det var så lidt" means "you're welcome" or "don't mention it". Word for word, it says it was so little, as if the favor was nothing. It is a warm answer when someone thanks you.

forms.da: Tak for hjælpen! – Det var så lidt.
forms.en: Thanks for the help! – Don't mention it.

sentence.da: Tak for hjælpen! **Det var så lidt.**
sentence.en: Thanks for the help! Don't mention it.

det ved jeg ikke.explanation: "Det ved jeg ikke" means "I don't know". Det (that) comes first, then ved jeg (know I). At vide (to know) is for facts; for knowing a person or place use at kende (to be familiar with).

forms.da: Det ved jeg ikke noget om.

sentence.da: Hvor er Peter? **Det ved jeg ikke.**
sentence.en: Where is Peter? I don't know.

det vil sige.explanation: "Det vil sige" means "that is to say" and is used before you explain or sum up: Jeg bor i Jylland, det vil sige i Aarhus (I live in Jutland, that is to say in Aarhus). In writing it is often shortened to dvs. (i.e.)

forms.da: Det vil sige, at du kommer
forms.en: That is to say, you are coming

sentence.da: Vi mødes klokken otte, **det vil sige** om en time.
sentence.en: We meet at eight, that is to say in an hour.

detaljeret.explanation: "Detaljeret" means "detailed", giving many small parts, not just the main points. Its opposite is overfladisk (superficial), which only touches the surface.

sentence.da: Kortet er meget **detaljeret**, og man kan se hver eneste sti.
sentence.en: The map is very detailed, and you can see every single path.

dets.explanation: "Dets" means "its" and belongs to something that is an et-word, such as et æble (an apple). For an en-word, like a car, use dens.

sentence.da: Huset er gammelt, men **dets** tag er nyt.
sentence.en: The house is old, but its roof is new.

dette.explanation: "Dette" means "this" with a word that takes et. With a word that takes en, use denne: denne bil (this car). It sounds a bit formal; in everyday speech Danes say det her: Jeg vil have det her (I want this one).

sentence.da: Jeg vil købe **dette** hus.
sentence.en: I want to buy this house.

diabetes.explanation: "Diabetes" means "diabetes", a long-term illness where the body cannot keep the sugar in the blood at a healthy level. In everyday talk, Danes also say sukkersyge (sugar sickness).

sentence.da: Han har **diabetes** og tager insulin hver dag.
sentence.en: He has diabetes and takes insulin every day.

diarré.explanation: "Diarré" means "diarrhea", an upset stomach where the stool is watery and you need the toilet often. It often comes with mavesyge (a stomach bug).

sentence.da: Man kan få **diarré** af dårlig mad.
sentence.en: You can get diarrhea from bad food.

diesel.explanation: "Diesel" means "diesel", a fuel used by many vans and trucks. Do not mix it up with benzin (gasoline).

sentence.da: Varebilen kører på **diesel**, ikke på benzin.
sentence.en: The van runs on diesel, not on gasoline.

dig.explanation: "Dig" means "you" when something is done to you. Du is the one who does it: Du elsker mig (You love me). Dig is also used after little words like med (with): Jeg kommer med dig (I am coming with you). Dig is for one person; for several people say jer (you, many).

sentence.da: Jeg kan høre **dig**.
sentence.en: I can hear you.

digital.explanation: "Digital" means "digital", for things that work electronically and show numbers instead of hands, such as a clock. It looks like the English word, but the stress is on the last part: di-gi-TAL.

sentence.da: Uret er **digital** og viser tiden med tal.
sentence.en: The watch is digital and shows the time with numbers.

dild.explanation: "Dild" means "dill", a green herb with thin, feathery leaves, often used with fish and new potatoes.

sentence.da: Fisken smager godt med **dild**.
sentence.en: The fish tastes good with dill.

din.explanation: "Din" means "your" or "yours" when you talk to one person and the thing takes en. For a thing that takes et, it is dit: dit hus (your house). For more than one thing, it is dine: dine sko (your shoes).

sentence.da: Her er **din** kaffe.
sentence.en: Here is your coffee.

dine.explanation: "Dine" means "your" or "yours" when there is more than one thing. For one thing, it is din or dit: din sko (your shoe), dit hus (your house).

sentence.da: Tag **dine** sko på.
sentence.en: Put your shoes on.

diplomatisk.explanation: "Diplomatisk" means "diplomatic", both for relations between countries and for handling a touchy situation with care: Vær diplomatisk (Be diplomatic).

sentence.da: Hun var **diplomatisk** og sagde det på en venlig måde.
sentence.en: She was diplomatic and said it in a friendly way.

direkte.explanation: "Direkte" means "directly" and also "direct". Both mean going straight, with nothing in between: et direkte tog (a direct train) has no stops on the way.

sentence.da: Jeg tager **direkte** hjem efter arbejde.
sentence.en: I go straight home after work.

disciplin.explanation: "En disciplin" means "a discipline". It is self-control, as in Hun har stor disciplin (She has great discipline), and it is also one single event within a sport.

sentence.da: Hundrede meter er en **disciplin** ved de olympiske lege.
sentence.en: The hundred meters is an event at the Olympic Games.

diset.explanation: "Diset" means "hazy", for air that is full of thin mist so that distant things look soft and pale. It is lighter than tåget (foggy), where you can barely see anything.

sentence.da: Morgenen var **diset**, og vi kunne næsten ikke se bjergene.
sentence.en: The morning was hazy, and we could hardly see the mountains.

diskret.explanation: "Diskret" means "discreet", not drawing attention to itself. For a person it means keeping private things private, and for a thing it means small and quiet in style: en diskret farve (a subtle color).

sentence.da: Hun er **diskret** og fortæller aldrig andres hemmeligheder.
sentence.en: She is discreet and never tells other people's secrets.

diskrimination.explanation: "Diskrimination" means "discrimination", treating people worse because of who they are. The reason is often given with på grund af (because of): diskrimination på grund af alder (discrimination because of age).

sentence.da: **Diskrimination** er, når nogen bliver behandlet dårligere på grund af deres køn.
sentence.en: Discrimination is when someone is treated worse because of their gender.

disse.explanation: "Disse" means "these". For one thing, it is denne or dette: denne sko (this shoe), dette hus (this house). It sounds a bit formal; in everyday speech, Danes say de her: de her sko (these shoes).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **disse** sko.
sentence.en: I like these shoes.

distraheret.explanation: "Distraheret" means "distracted", unable to keep your mind on something because something else is pulling at it. The cause comes after af (by): Jeg var distraheret af min telefon (I was distracted by my phone).

sentence.da: Jeg er **distraheret**, fordi der er så meget støj.
sentence.en: I am distracted because there is so much noise.

dit.explanation: "Dit" means "your" or "yours" when you talk to one person and the thing takes et. For a thing that takes en, it is din: din bil (your car). For more than one thing, it is dine: dine sko (your shoes).

sentence.da: Hvad er **dit** navn?
sentence.en: What is your name?

dna.explanation: "Et DNA" means "DNA", the material inside living things that carries the plan for how they are built. In Danish it is read out letter by letter, as de-en-a.

sentence.da: **DNA** gør, at børn ligner deres forældre.
sentence.en: DNA makes children look like their parents.

dobbelt.explanation: "Dobbelt" means "double" and "twice as much". It starts many words, such as dobbeltværelse (double room).

sentence.da: Det koster **dobbelt** så meget i byen.
sentence.en: It costs twice as much in the city.

dog.explanation: "Dog" means "though", "still" or "anyway". It adds a little contrast: Det er dyrt, men jeg køber det dog (It is expensive, but I am buying it anyway). In a command, it makes the request friendlier: Kom dog ind! (Do come in!). It is not the same as men (but): Han er sød, men sur (He is sweet but grumpy).

sentence.da: Kom **dog** ind, Peter!
sentence.en: Do come in, Peter!

dokumentation.explanation: "En dokumentation" means "documentation", papers or text that show that something is true or explain how something works. Computer programs have it too: dokumentationen til programmet (the documentation for the program).

sentence.da: Kvitteringer er **dokumentation** for, hvad man har købt.
sentence.en: Receipts are documentation of what you have bought.

dommedag.explanation: "Dommedag" means "doomsday" or "Judgment Day", the last day of the world. People also use it for big trouble: Det er ikke dommedag (It is not the end of the world). It is built from dom (a verdict) and dag (day).

sentence.da: Ifølge kristendommen kommer **dommedag**, når Gud dømmer alle mennesker.
sentence.en: According to Christianity, Judgment Day comes when God judges all people.

doven.explanation: "Doven" means "lazy" and describes someone who avoids work. The opposite is flittig (diligent).

sentence.da: Han er **doven** og ligger i sofaen hele dagen.
sentence.en: He is lazy and lies on the sofa all day.

dramatisk.explanation: "Dramatisk" means "dramatic", for events that are sudden, big or exciting, such as a rescue or a storm. It can also describe someone who makes too much of things: Du er så dramatisk! (You are so dramatic!)

sentence.da: Det var en **dramatisk** redning, og alle holdt vejret.
sentence.en: It was a dramatic rescue, and everyone held their breath.

dressing.explanation: "En dressing" means "a dressing", the cold sauce you put on a salad. A warm sauce with meat is en sovs (a sauce) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg laver en **dressing** til salaten.
sentence.en: I make a dressing for the salad.

drikkepenge.explanation: "Drikkepenge" means "a tip", the extra money you give for good service. It is used without en or et: Tak, behold resten som drikkepenge (Thanks, keep the change as a tip).

sentence.da: Vi gav tjeneren **drikkepenge**, fordi maden var god.
sentence.en: We gave the waiter a tip because the food was good.

drikkevarer.explanation: "Drikkevarer" means "drinks" or "beverages" as a group, like on a menu or in a shop. For one single drink, say en drik: en kold drik (a cold drink).

sentence.da: Vi sælger mad og **drikkevarer** i kiosken.
sentence.en: We sell food and drinks in the kiosk.

dristig.explanation: "Dristig" means "bold" or "daring", ready to try something that others hold back from. For clothes it means a little shocking: en dristig kjole (a daring dress).

sentence.da: En **dristig** person tør tage chancer, som andre ikke tør.
sentence.en: A bold person dares to take chances that others do not dare to.

du.explanation: "Du" means "you" when you talk to one person: Du er sød (You are sweet). Danes use it with almost everyone, even older people and your boss. When something is done to you, it is dig: Jeg ser dig (I see you). When you talk to several people, say I: I er søde (You are all sweet).

sentence.da: Hvor bor **du**?
sentence.en: Where do you live?

dug.explanation: "En dug" means "dew", the tiny beads of water that form outdoors on cool nights. The same spelling is also a different word, en dug (a tablecloth): en hvid dug (a white tablecloth).

sentence.da: Om morgenen ligger der **dug** på græsset.
sentence.en: In the morning there is dew on the grass.

dum.explanation: "Dum" means "stupid" or "silly". Said about a person, it can sound rude: Du er dum (You are stupid). About things, it is milder: Det var dumt (That was silly).

sentence.da: Det var en **dum** fejl.
sentence.en: That was a stupid mistake.

dyb.explanation: "Dyb" means "deep", as in deep water or a deep hole. It also works for sleep and voices: en dyb søvn (a deep sleep), en dyb stemme (a deep voice).

sentence.da: Søen er for **dyb** til børn.
sentence.en: The lake is too deep for children.

dybtgående.explanation: "Dybtgående" means "thorough" or "profound", for something that goes far down and not only on the surface. It is built from dybt (deeply) and gående (going), and is used for studies, knowledge and changes.

sentence.da: En **dybtgående** undersøgelse tager lang tid, men den finder de skjulte fejl.
sentence.en: A thorough investigation takes a long time, but it finds the hidden errors.

dygtig.explanation: "Dygtig" means "skilled" or "capable", good at what you do: Hun er dygtig til sprog (She is good at languages). Dygtig! is also a way to say "Well done!"

sentence.da: Han er **dygtig** og lærer hurtigt.
sentence.en: He is capable and learns quickly.

dynamisk.explanation: "Dynamisk" means "dynamic", full of energy and ready to change, for people, groups and places.

sentence.da: Firmaet er **dynamisk** og ændrer sig hele tiden.
sentence.en: The company is dynamic and keeps changing all the time.

dyr.explanation: "Dyr" means "expensive". Be careful: et dyr is a different word that means "an animal".

sentence.da: Jakken koster 5000 kroner. Den er meget **dyr**.
sentence.en: The jacket costs 5000 kroner. It is very expensive.

dyrebar.explanation: "Dyrebar" means "precious", worth a great deal to you. It grows out of dyr (expensive), but it is more about feeling or rarity than about a price: Tid er dyrebar (Time is precious).

sentence.da: Mormors gamle ring er **dyrebar** for mig.
sentence.en: Grandma's old ring is precious to me.

dyrevelfærd.explanation: "Dyrevelfærd" means "animal welfare", how well animals are kept and treated. It is a common topic when people talk about farming.

sentence.da: God **dyrevelfærd** betyder, at dyrene har plads og får mad.
sentence.en: Good animal welfare means that the animals have room and get food.

dårlig.explanation: "Dårlig" means "bad", and it also means "unwell": Jeg har det dårligt means "I feel bad" or "I feel ill". The words for "worse" and "worst" are different: værre (worse) and værst (worst).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og har en **dårlig** dag.
sentence.en: I am sick and having a bad day.

dårlig til.explanation: "Dårlig til" means "bad at". After it you can name a skill, like matematik (math), or add at and an action, like at tegne (to draw).

forms.da: Jeg er dårlig til at lave mad.
Vi er dårlige til at danse.

sentence.da: Han er **dårlig til** at svømme, men han prøver.
sentence.en: He is bad at swimming, but he tries.

død.explanation: "Død" means "dead", for people, animals and plants. It is also used for things that have stopped working: Min telefon er død (My phone is dead).

sentence.da: Blomsten er **død** uden vand.
sentence.en: The flower is dead without water.

dødbringende.explanation: "Dødbringende" means "deadly", able to cause death. It is built from død (death) and bringende (bringing). Dødelig (deadly) also means "mortal", about people who can die, but dødbringende only describes what causes death.

sentence.da: Slangens bid er **dødbringende**, når man ikke får modgift hurtigt.
sentence.en: The snake's bite is deadly when you do not get an antidote quickly.

dødelig.explanation: "Dødelig" means "deadly" when something can kill, and "mortal" when someone can die: Vi er alle dødelige (We are all mortal).

sentence.da: Giften fra slangen er **dødelig** for mennesker.
sentence.en: The venom from the snake is deadly to humans.

dødkedelig.explanation: "Dødkedelig" means "deadly boring", extremely dull. Danish often puts død- (dead) in front of a word to make it extreme, as in dødtræt (dead tired).

sentence.da: Filmen var **dødkedelig**, og jeg faldt i søvn.
sentence.en: The movie was deadly boring, and I fell asleep.

dødsstraf.explanation: "En dødsstraf" means "a death penalty", the punishment of being put to death by the state. The usual verb is at idømme (to impose): idømme dødsstraf (to impose the death penalty).

sentence.da: **Dødsstraf** er den hårdeste straf, en stat kan give.
sentence.en: The death penalty is the harshest punishment a state can give.

dømmekraft.explanation: "En dømmekraft" means "judgment", the ability to weigh things up and decide wisely. It is about being sensible, not about a court: a court gives en dom (a verdict).

sentence.da: Når man har **dømmekraft**, tænker man sig om, før man beslutter noget.
sentence.en: When you have judgment, you think before you decide anything.

døv.explanation: "Døv" means "deaf", not able to hear. Someone who hears a little is hørehæmmet (hard of hearing).

sentence.da: Hun er født **døv** og taler med hænderne.
sentence.en: She was born deaf and talks with her hands.

en dag.explanation: "En dag" means "a day", as in hver dag (every day) and god dag (hello, good day). The days of the week end in -dag, for example mandag (Monday) and tirsdag (Tuesday).

sentence.da: Mandag er den første **dag** i ugen.
sentence.en: Monday is the first day of the week.

en dagbog.explanation: "En dagbog" means "a diary", a book where you write about your own days. It is built from dag (day) and bog (book). You say at føre dagbog (to keep a diary).

sentence.da: Hun skriver hver aften i sin **dagbog**.
sentence.en: She writes in her diary every evening.

en daglig leder.explanation: "En daglig leder" means "a general manager". Literally it is a daily leader: the person who runs a company, shop or department every day.

sentence.da: Han er både ejer og **daglig leder** af butikken.
sentence.en: He is both the owner and general manager of the shop.

en dagligvare.explanation: "En dagligvare" means "a grocery item", a thing you buy often for daily life, like bread or soap. It is mostly used in the plural: dagligvarer (groceries).

sentence.da: Mælk er en **dagligvare**, som vi køber hver uge.
sentence.en: Milk is a grocery item that we buy every week.

en dagplejer.explanation: "En dagplejer" means "a home daycare provider", a person who looks after small children in their own home during the day. Many Danish towns offer it for the youngest children, as an alternative to en vuggestue (a daycare center for toddlers).

sentence.da: Vores søn er hos en **dagplejer**, mens vi arbejder.
sentence.en: Our son is with a home daycare provider while we work.

en dagsorden.explanation: "En dagsorden" means "an agenda", the list of topics for a meeting, in the order they will be taken up. It is also used in a wider sense: noget er på dagsordenen (something is on the agenda) means it is being discussed in society.

sentence.da: Før mødet sender lederen en **dagsorden** til alle.
sentence.en: Before the meeting, the manager sends an agenda to everyone.

en dagsrejse.explanation: "En dagsrejse" means "a day trip", going out and back in one day. It is built from dag (day) and rejse (journey), and rejse is also a verb: at rejse (to travel).

sentence.da: Vi tager på en **dagsrejse** og er hjemme i aften.
sentence.en: We go on a day trip and are home tonight.

en dal.explanation: "En dal" means "a valley", low land between higher ground.

sentence.da: Floden løber gennem en smuk **dal**.
sentence.en: The river runs through a beautiful valley.

en dam.explanation: "En dam" means "a pond", a small body of still water. A bigger one is en sø (a lake).

sentence.da: Der bor mange frøer i den lille **dam**.
sentence.en: Many frogs live in the little pond.

en dame.explanation: "En dame" means "a lady", a polite word for a woman. You often see Damer on a restroom door, meaning the women's restroom. Mine damer og herrer means "Ladies and gentlemen".

sentence.da: En pige bliver til en **dame**.
sentence.en: A girl becomes a lady.

en dannelse.explanation: "En dannelse" means "an education", but in the sense of personal and cultural growth, like good manners and wide knowledge. For school or job training, use en uddannelse (a training program). It can also mean "formation", how something comes into being: dannelsen af skyer (the formation of clouds).

sentence.da: **Dannelse** handler om manerer og viden, ikke om eksamener.
sentence.en: Cultural education is about manners and knowledge, not about exams.

en dans.explanation: "En dans" means "a dance", a set of steps done to music. The action is at danse (to dance).

sentence.da: Jeg har lært en ny **dans** til festen.
sentence.en: I have learned a new dance for the party.

en danser.explanation: "En danser" means "a dancer", a person who dances, for fun or as a job.

sentence.da: Hun er en god **danser**, og hun øver hver dag.
sentence.en: She is a good dancer, and she practices every day.

en dansker.explanation: "En dansker" means "a Dane", a person from Denmark. The word is the same for men and women. To say what nationality someone is, Danish leaves out en: Han er dansker means "He is a Dane".

sentence.da: Han bor i Danmark og er **dansker**.
sentence.en: He lives in Denmark and is a Dane.

en danskuddannelse.explanation: "En danskuddannelse" means "a Danish course (for adults)", the official Danish teaching for foreigners who live in Denmark. It comes in three levels, called danskuddannelse 1, 2 and 3, depending on the learner's school background.

sentence.da: Hun tager en **danskuddannelse** på sprogcentret to gange om ugen.
sentence.en: She takes a Danish course at the language center twice a week.

en dataanalytiker.explanation: "En dataanalytiker" means "a data analyst", a person who works with large amounts of data in a company or public office and turns it into advice for others.

sentence.da: En **dataanalytiker** undersøger tal for at finde mønstre.
sentence.en: A data analyst examines numbers to find patterns.

en database.explanation: "En database" means "a database", a place where a company or a program keeps lots of information.

sentence.da: Vi gemmer alle navne i en **database**.
sentence.en: We save all the names in a database.

en date.explanation: "En date" means "a date", a romantic meeting between two people. It is not a date on the calendar. That is en dato (a calendar date).

sentence.da: Han har en **date** i aften og er meget nervøs.
sentence.en: He has a date tonight and is very nervous.

en dato.explanation: "En dato" means "a date" on the calendar, such as 5 March. Do not mix it up with a romantic date, which is en date (borrowed from English).

sentence.da: Hvilken **dato** er det i dag?
sentence.en: What date is it today?

en datter.explanation: "En datter" means "a daughter", a girl or woman seen as the child of her parents. She stays a datter when she is grown up.

sentence.da: Jeg har en søn og en **datter**.
sentence.en: I have a son and a daughter.

en deadline.explanation: "En deadline" means "a deadline", the last moment by which something must be finished, for work or school. Danish also has en frist (a time limit).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **deadline** på fredag.
sentence.en: I have a deadline on Friday.

en debat.explanation: "En debat" means "a debate", an exchange of opinions on television, in newspapers or online. It usually has some order, unlike et skænderi (a quarrel).

sentence.da: Der var en lang **debat** om skolen i fjernsynet i går.
sentence.en: There was a long debate about the school on TV yesterday.

en debattør.explanation: "En debattør" means "a debater", a person who often takes part in public discussion by writing in newspapers or speaking on television. The word is built from en debat (a debate).

sentence.da: Som kendt **debattør** skriver hun ofte om politik i aviserne.
sentence.en: As a well-known debater, she often writes about politics in the newspapers.

en debut.explanation: "En debut" means "a debut", the first time a person shows their work or skill to the public, such as a singer's first album or a player's first match. The matching verb is at debutere (to make your debut).

sentence.da: Hendes **debut** som forfatter var en roman om barndommen.
sentence.en: Her debut as a writer was a novel about childhood.

en deciliter.explanation: "En deciliter" means "a deciliter", one tenth of a liter, often used in recipes. Danish recipes write it as dl: 2 dl mel (2 deciliters of flour).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger to **deciliter** mel i brødet.
sentence.en: I use two deciliters of flour in the bread.

en definition.explanation: "En definition" means "a definition", an exact explanation of what a word means: Hvad er definitionen på frihed? (What is the definition of freedom?). The word after på says which word is being defined.

sentence.da: Jeg kender ikke ordets **definition**.
sentence.en: I do not know the definition of the word.

en dej.explanation: "En dej" means "a dough", the soft mix of flour and liquid you make before baking. It covers both thick bread dough and runny pancake mix.

sentence.da: Jeg laver **dej** af mel og vand.
sentence.en: I make dough from flour and water.

en dekoration.explanation: "En dekoration" means "a decoration", something that makes a room or a table look nicer. The action is at dekorere (to decorate).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **dekoration** til bordet.
sentence.en: I am buying a decoration for the table.

en del.explanation: "En del" means "a part": Det er en del af planen (It is part of the plan). It also means "quite a lot": Der er en del mennesker her (There are quite a few people here).

sentence.da: Musik er en stor **del** af mit liv.
sentence.en: Music is a big part of my life.

en delfin.explanation: "En delfin" means "a dolphin", a smart sea animal that jumps out of the water.

sentence.da: En **delfin** bor i havet og spiser fisk.
sentence.en: A dolphin lives in the sea and eats fish.

en delmængde.explanation: "En delmængde" means "a subset", a group whose members all also belong to a bigger group. It is used mostly in math.

sentence.da: Lige tal er en **delmængde** af de hele tal.
sentence.en: Even numbers are a subset of the whole numbers.

en deltager.explanation: "En deltager" means "a participant", someone who takes part in something. It comes from at deltage (to take part).

sentence.da: Hver **deltager** får en lille gave.
sentence.en: Each participant gets a small gift.

en deltagerliste.explanation: "En deltagerliste" means "a list of participants". It is built from en deltager (a participant) and en liste (a list), and liste is also in en indkøbsliste (a shopping list).

sentence.da: Der er tyve navne på vores **deltagerliste**.
sentence.en: There are twenty names on our participant list.

en demonstration.explanation: "En demonstration" means "a demonstration" in two ways: a gathering or march where people publicly show what they want, and a showing of how something works. In daily speech, it is often shortened to en demo (a demo).

sentence.da: Tusindvis af mennesker gik til **demonstration** foran Christiansborg.
sentence.en: Thousands of people went to a demonstration in front of Christiansborg.

en deodorant.explanation: "En deodorant" means "a deodorant", something you put under your arms to stop bad smells. When you talk about using it in general, Danes usually leave out en: Har du deodorant? (Do you have deodorant?).

sentence.da: Jeg lugter ikke, fordi jeg bruger **deodorant**.
sentence.en: I do not smell bad, because I use deodorant.

en depression.explanation: "En depression" means "a depression", a serious illness in which a person feels very sad, empty and without energy for weeks or longer. For a short low mood, Danes say nedtrykt (feeling down).

sentence.da: Når man har en **depression**, mister man ofte lysten til alt.
sentence.en: When you have depression, you often lose interest in everything.

en designer.explanation: "En designer" means "a designer", someone who plans how things look, such as clothes, furniture or websites.

sentence.da: Hun er **designer** og laver smukt tøj.
sentence.en: She is a designer and makes beautiful clothes.

en dessert.explanation: "En dessert" means "a dessert", the sweet dish at the end of a meal. It is spelled like the English word, with two s's. A desert (dry land) is en ørken.

sentence.da: Efter maden vil jeg have en **dessert**.
sentence.en: After the meal I want a dessert.

en destination.explanation: "En destination" means "a destination", the place a traveler is heading to.

sentence.da: Vores **destination** er en lille by ved havet.
sentence.en: Our destination is a small town by the sea.

en detalje.explanation: "En detalje" means "a detail", a small part of something bigger. The phrase i detaljer (in detail) goes with explaining: Hun forklarede alt i detaljer (She explained everything in detail).

sentence.da: Billedet er flot, men én **detalje** er forkert.
sentence.en: The picture is nice, but one detail is wrong.

en detektiv.explanation: "En detektiv" means "a detective", a person who finds out who did a crime. A private one is en privatdetektiv (a private detective).

sentence.da: En **detektiv** leder efter spor på gerningsstedet.
sentence.en: A detective looks for clues at the crime scene.

en detektor.explanation: "En detektor" means "a detector", a device that senses something and gives a signal: en metaldetektor (a metal detector). A person who solves crimes is not en detektor but en detektiv (a detective).

sentence.da: En **detektor** i loftet giver alarm, hvis der er røg.
sentence.en: A detector in the ceiling sounds the alarm if there is smoke.

en diagnose.explanation: "En diagnose" means "a diagnosis", the name a doctor gives to an illness after checking a patient, for example influenza or diabetes. To make one is at stille en diagnose (to make a diagnosis).

sentence.da: Når man har fået en **diagnose**, kan lægen vælge en behandling.
sentence.en: Once you have a diagnosis, the doctor can choose a treatment.

en dialekt.explanation: "En dialekt" means "a dialect", the way people speak in one region, with its own sounds and some of its own words. Examples are sønderjysk (from South Jutland) and bornholmsk (from Bornholm).

sentence.da: Mormor taler en **dialekt**, som jeg næsten ikke forstår.
sentence.en: Grandma speaks a dialect that I hardly understand.

en dialog.explanation: "En dialog" means "a dialogue", a talk between two people, as written in a book, play or film. It also describes an open exchange of views between groups, such as politicians and citizens: at føre en dialog (to hold a dialogue).

sentence.da: Der er meget **dialog** og lidt handling i stykket.
sentence.en: There is a lot of dialogue and little action in the play.

en diamant.explanation: "En diamant" means "a diamond", a clear, valuable stone used in jewelry. The diamond in playing cards is called ruder (diamonds), not diamant.

sentence.da: En **diamant** er så hård, at den kan skære i glas.
sentence.en: A diamond is so hard that it can cut glass.

en diameter.explanation: "En diameter" means "a diameter", the distance straight across a circle, going through the middle. It is twice as long as en radius (a radius).

sentence.da: Pizzaen har en **diameter** på tredive centimeter.
sentence.en: The pizza has a diameter of thirty centimeters.

en digter.explanation: "En digter" means "a poet", a person who writes verse. H.C. Andersen is often called en digter, even though he is best known for his fairy tales.

sentence.da: En **digter** skriver digte om kærlighed, natur og livet.
sentence.en: A poet writes poems about love, nature and life.

en digtsamling.explanation: "En digtsamling" means "a poetry collection", a book that gathers many poems. A book with poems by several writers is instead called en antologi (an anthology).

sentence.da: I en **digtsamling** står der mange digte af samme digter.
sentence.en: In a poetry collection there are many poems by the same poet.

en diktat.explanation: "En diktat" means "a dictation", a text that one person says out loud while another writes it down, for example when a manager reads out a letter to a secretary.

sentence.da: Til **diktat** skriver eleverne ned, hvad læreren læser højt.
sentence.en: In dictation the students write down what the teacher reads aloud.

en diktator.explanation: "En diktator" means "a dictator", a ruler who holds all the power in a country. The system is called et diktatur (a dictatorship).

sentence.da: I et land med en **diktator** er der ingen frie valg.
sentence.en: In a country with a dictator there are no free elections.

en dimension.explanation: "En dimension" means "a dimension", a direction in which you can measure something. It is also used for a side of a problem or an experience: det giver sagen en ny dimension (that gives the matter a new dimension).

sentence.da: Længde er en **dimension**, ligesom bredde og højde.
sentence.en: Length is a dimension, just like width and height.

en diplomat.explanation: "En diplomat" means "a diplomat", a person who represents the country abroad and negotiates with other governments, often working at an embassy. It also describes a tactful person in daily life: Hun er en rigtig diplomat (She is a real diplomat).

sentence.da: Som **diplomat** bor han i udlandet og taler for sit land.
sentence.en: As a diplomat, he lives abroad and speaks for his country.

en direktør.explanation: "En direktør" means "a director" or "a CEO", the top manager of a company. A person who guides a smaller team is en leder (a leader).

sentence.da: Firmaets **direktør** er chef for alle de ansatte.
sentence.en: The company's director is the boss of all the employees.

en dirigent.explanation: "En dirigent" means "a conductor", the person who leads an orchestra or a choir with movements of the arms and hands. For the person who checks tickets on a train, Danes say en konduktør (a ticket inspector).

sentence.da: En **dirigent** viser orkestret, hvornår det skal spille højt.
sentence.en: A conductor shows the orchestra when to play loudly.

en disharmoni.explanation: "En disharmoni" means "a discord", sounds that do not fit together in music, or a lack of peace between people.

sentence.da: Efter skænderiet var der **disharmoni** i hele familien.
sentence.en: After the quarrel, there was discord in the whole family.

en diskussion.explanation: "En diskussion" means "a discussion", people talking about a topic and sharing different opinions.

sentence.da: Vi havde en **diskussion** om, hvem der skulle betale.
sentence.en: We had a discussion about who should pay.

en diæt.explanation: "En diæt" means "a diet", a special way of eating for a certain time, often to get thinner or because of an illness. For the food you normally eat, Danes say kost (food habits): en sund kost (a healthy diet).

sentence.da: Lægen anbefalede mig en **diæt** uden sukker.
sentence.en: The doctor recommended a sugar-free diet to me.

en djævel.explanation: "En djævel" means "a devil", an evil being in religion and stories. In daily speech it is also used about a person: en stakkels djævel (a poor devil) is someone you feel sorry for.

sentence.da: I mange billeder har en **djævel** horn og en lang hale.
sentence.en: In many pictures, a devil has horns and a long tail.

en doktor.explanation: "En doktor" means "a doctor", but in everyday Danish people mostly say en læge (a medical doctor). Still, Jeg skal til doktoren (I am going to the doctor) is fine in casual speech.

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og skal til **doktor** Hansen.
sentence.en: I am sick and going to Doctor Hansen.

en dokumentar.explanation: "En dokumentar" means "a documentary", a film about real events or real people, not a made-up story.

sentence.da: En **dokumentar** viser, hvordan pandaer lever i naturen.
sentence.en: A documentary shows how pandas live in the wild.

en dollar.explanation: "En dollar" means "a dollar", the currency used in the United States and some other countries.

sentence.da: I USA betaler man med **dollar**.
sentence.en: In the USA you pay with dollars.

en dom.explanation: "En dom" means "a verdict", the decision a court gives at the end of a case. It also covers the punishment itself: Han fik en dom på tre års fængsel (He got a sentence of three years in prison).

sentence.da: Retten afsagde **dom** i sagen i går.
sentence.en: The court gave its verdict in the case yesterday.

en dommer.explanation: "En dommer" means "a judge", the person who decides a case in court. In sports it also means "a referee": Dommeren blæste i fløjten (The referee blew the whistle).

sentence.da: I retten bestemmer en **dommer** straffen.
